utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know that last name, Vrkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that Mr. Badzim gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in March of this year?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that in his statement he says: In June of 2009, Mr. Bajic, the state attorney of Croatia, ordered an investigation into command responsibility for Grubori by the crime police, current crime police?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: I have no information to that effect. I have no information about any interviews of Mr. Badzim either. And I'm not familiar with the piece of information you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the 2001 investigation into Grubori, conducted by Mr. Zganjer?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: Only from the existing files that were used to carry out an analysis. Based on that, I was able to draw a conclusion that there was a criminal investigation underway in 2001, although I did not participate in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you shed any light into why, from 2001 until the middle of this case here in The Hague, no investigation was conducted like the one that's being conducted now into Grubori?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Other than Mr. Vrticevic and Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Djurica, from whom else have you taken Official Notes? You or Mr. Gerovac. Related to Grubori.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: I don't know. During the criminal investigation, there was a number of interviews; at least 20, 30, maybe even 40. I can't be precise. And not all of them were conducted jointly with Mr. Gerovac. There were several of us on the team, and it all depended on the roster. I cannot be precise as to the exact number of the interviews and who those interviews were conducted with. I cannot tell you the specific names. But it is easy enough to ascertain if you look into the files.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you shed any light on what led you or Mr. Badzim - or, for that matter, Mr. Gerovac, if you know - to Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: I think we carried out a criminal analysis of the previous activities undertaken in relation to Grubori. Precisely, it was the investigation in 2001 that we considered. Based on that, we drafted a work-plan which we later on followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether, in that material of 2001, Mr. Vrticevic and/or Mr. Bilobrk were either interviewed or mentioned by anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question. I did not have the 2001 file.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, it's not only because of the time but also because of the way in which the cross-examination develops that I would urge you to see -- to come to the most relevant questions and see whether you could finish in a relatively short time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No need to re-examine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one brief question for you, Mr. Mikulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell me -- you conducted the interview with Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic on a Thursday, the 5th of November. The Official Note was put on paper and signed on the 9th of November, the Monday following. Do you remember the persons you interviewed between that Thursday and that Monday?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: I can't recall the names of those people, but I think that there was an interview, after Mr. Bilobrk's interview, which we had in Split. I think it was scheduled for 5.00 or 6.00 p.m. And on and Friday, in Zadar, we had another two or three interviews, but I cannot recall with whom. There were too many interviews, and I'd rather not speculate. However, I'm basically positive about this number of interviews I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll tell you the reason why I asked you and see whether you can further assist in what is on my mind. I was asking myself to what extent any interviews you may have conducted between the 5th and the 9th of November may have contaminated the Official Note which was put on paper. That is to say, that you would have mixed up any information you heard during those days, which would then possibly have ended up in the Official Note of the 9th of November. Having explained this, do you remember what the subjects were of the interviews you conducted in those days?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: The topic was sanitation and hygiene measures undertaken concerning Grubori. Those people, in a way, could have been in a position to provide information, be it directly or indirectly, about those events or first-hand or second-hand information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether, during those interviews, the issue of suggested putting weapons close to the bodies was part of the questions that were put during those interviews? If you remember. If you don't remember, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO MIKULIC
utterances.text: I do not remember. However, I don't think it was mentioned in those interviews.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no further questions for you. Have the questions of the Bench triggered any need for further examination? Mr. Mikulic, this concludes your testimony in this Court. Nevertheless, we would like you to remain stand by. We hear evidence on specific issues, and it may well be that since you're now in The Hague, that we would profit from your presence if the other evidence we hear today or we -- we hear today would be in need of further clarification. Therefore, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in any other way with anyone about the testimony you've given. And I would like to ask you to remain stand by. You may have been informed about this procedure already by the Victims and Witness Section. You are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any questions in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you will be informed by the Victims and Witness Section whether, at what moment, we would not need you anymore, if we don't call you -- re-call you, and that would mean that once you have received that message you are free again to speak with whomever you want about everything, including your testimony, but not at this moment. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness -- I already, in case we do not see you again today, I already would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench. And, again, if we do not see each other later today, I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, no protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The Prosecution would like to call Witness 177, Antonio Gerovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the usher is already invited to bring Mr. Gerovac into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the parties provide numbers of exhibits which they intend to use to the Registrar so that hard copies will be prepared. And that is both for Prosecution and for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Gerovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you by the usher. Could you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gerovac. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, you'll first be examined by Mr. Hedaraly. Mr. Hedaraly is counsel for the Prosecution. He is at your right. You may proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Gerovac.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I understand that you also speak English. So if there's any need or if you ever prefer to hear the questions in its original form, just please feel free to ask. Can you please first state your full name and date of birth for the record.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: My name is Antonio Gerovac. I was born on the 25th of July, 1974.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I'm a police official in charge of homicides with the general administration of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Starting in 2009, were you involved in the investigation of the killings in Grubori that occurred in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And can you tell us briefly what that work entails.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Our work meant that we were supposed to carry out an analysis of the existing file, which came about as the result of an investigation by some other colleagues of ours who had previously worked on the case. Having done that, we drafted a detailed work-plan, which stipulated specific measure be under taken, and we were supposed to follow the plan in terms of carrying out interviews and all other investigative aspects that figured in that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. As part of this investigation, did you interview two forensic technicians in November 2009: Mr. Jozo Bilobrk, and Mr. Ivica Vrticevic?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Had Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic been interviewed previously by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes, they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you review the -- the reports or the Official Notes from these interviews before you interviewed Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court, please, what led you to re-interview Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: The first interview that was carried out with the two colleagues came about because they were jointly mentioned in a single Official Note, which is contrary to all professional rules. Secondly, myself and the colleagues working on that case, we believed that this was not a quality interview in the sense that no answers were received to the specific questions, and the questions were not sufficiently good either. It was impermissible that they were interviewed jointly in the same room and that their statements formed part of a single Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me just show you briefly those prior notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can have P2731, P2730, and P2734 provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And can you just confirm that these are the prior interview notes that you reviewed before your interview with Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you. [Interpretation] Yes, these are the Official Notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you interviewed Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic - and I'm now talking about them jointly; but whenever it's appropriate, we can separate them - did you come to learn any evidence that was not previously in the possession of your investigation team?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We learned of a fact -- or, rather, we learned of what Mr. Bilobrk clarified when he said that during the morning - and I don't know whether it was on the 26th or the 27th of August, 1995 - in any case, immediately prior to leaving to Grubori to carry out the clearing of terrain operation, as they were seated in front of the police administration in Knin, General Cermak appeared, escorted by a number of other employees of the ministry. He suggested to Mr. Bilobrk that prior to going to Grubori the scene of crime should be corrupted by portraying an imagine of combat which would have taken place. He responded by stating that he did not wish to work that way. After that, General Cermak turn around and left with the group he had come with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me just take you back in time just a little bit. Before your interview with Mr. Bilobrk and with Mr. Vrticevic, did you come do learn of this -- did anyone else mention this fact to you that Mr. Bilobrk, you say, clarified for you?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps to make it clearer, he didn't say this to me specifically but -- but to Mr. Mikulic. I don't know when exactly, but before we discussed this with Vrticevic and Bilobrk, Mikulic discussed the issue with Mr. Franjo Djurica, who, if I'm not mistaken, was a part of the Defence team, in an informal conversation. That was after the interview was carried out by Mr. Mikulic and Ilijas with Mr. Djurica. Unofficially, he then stated that in conversation with Mr. Bilobrk and Vrticevic, he learned of what I just shared with you. The two of them spoke about the event involving Mr. Cermak when interviewed by him. They also undertook to contact either him or someone from the Defence team should anyone ask of them to provide any further statement -- statements. However, he also said that he would never repeat the same words and that he would never acknowledge having said that, and that is why he was not made part of the Official Note. We used this only as an operational piece of information or intelligence, and we did not include it into the Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, you said that Mr. -- Mr. Franjo did not say that to you but to your colleagues. How did you find out what Mr. Franjo had told your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, look, every day the Working Group held a morning meeting at which tasks were issued to the individual members of the team. Later on, the team would gather again during a coordination meeting, towards the end of the day, where we again shared the information of that day with the rest of the Working Group. This is how we received or learned of this piece of information, at one of the meetings following the interview with Mr. Franjo Djurica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want to move to the interviews that you and your colleague Mr. Mikulic conducted with Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic. First of all, were they both interviewed on the same day?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were they interviewed together or separately?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Who did you interview first?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you remember where you conducted that interview?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes. In the premises of the police administration of Split-Dalmatia, if I'm not mistaken, in the Department of Forensics, in Vrticevic's office, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when and where did you interview Mr. Bilobrk?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: We interviewed Mr. Bilobrk the same day following the interview with Mr. Vrticevic. Also in the premises of the Split-Dalmatia Police Administration in the department for general crime, in one of the offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So in a different location from where you interviewed Mr. Vrticevic; in a different office in the same building. Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes, you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Bilobrk from before?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I did. We were acquaintances or work-mates. We had met a number of times before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Was your interview with Mr. Bilobrk formal or informal?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: It was formal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "a formal interview"?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: We interviewed Mr. Bilobrk officially about the events and his knowledge about what happened after the killing of civilians in the village of Grubori. In other words, we interviewed him about the knowledge he had concerning the events that unfolded after the killing of the civilians in Grubori.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I -- I think I -- I think I asked you a bad question. What do you mean by a formal interview, as opposed to an informal interview, generally. What's the difference?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: You see, when an official interview is conducted - and perhaps this is a rather clumsy formulation - it is normally followed by an Official Note. At such an interview, the individual interviewed is acquainted with the reasons why he or she was invited there. The person is interviewed. And at the end of the interview, an Official Note is made, which is not a form of evidence but is an accurate reflection of someone's words.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you inform Mr. Bilobrk that the interview that you wanted to conduct with him was formal?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We told him what the topic of our interview will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what was that topic? I know you may have said it earlier, but if you don't mind repeating it. What did you tell him the topic of the interview was?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: We told him that the topic of our conversation was going be to the killing of civilians in Grubori and the knowledge he had about this incident and certain events that unfolded subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you remember what was the first question or questions that you put to Mr. Bilobrk in that interview?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: At first, we briefly informed Mr. Bilobrk that the criminal inquiries carried out so far had indicated that he and Mr. Vrticevic had not told the extent of their knowledge about the events in Grubori and that that was the reason why we summoned him again. The question put to him was whether, at that point in time, any of the highly positioned officers of MUP or the Ministry of Defence suggested that they place rifles next to the dead bodies so as to suggest that there had been combat taking place there. So that was the first of the questions that we put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Bilobrk's answer?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: As I've already said, Mr. Bilobrk said that in the morning General Cermak came in front of the MUP building in Knin, accompanied by certain individuals in uniform - he believed that they were his security detail - and that he suggested that next to the dead bodies in Grubori rifles be placed so as to make it seem as if a conflict had taken place there where these individuals had been killed and to suggest that resistance was mounted by the civilians in Grubori.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you at any point suggest Mr. Cermak as one of the individuals that may have made such a suggestion?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No, never. At no point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you -- can you explain to the Chamber why you didn't first ask a more general question to Mr. Bilobrk regarding, for example, what had happened in Grubori, if he had any information about -- something of a more general nature than that high-level officials may have made a suggestion such as this one?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, you see, two interviews had been conducted with Mr. Bilobrk by that point already. We believed that the area we focussed on was something that he had not been interviewed sufficiently on. Whereas, other information that he could provide we believed he had been questioned on sufficiently and that there was no reason for us to go into these areas. Although he did, in fact, repeat some of these issues gratuitously during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just to make absolutely clear: Who was the first person in the interview that mentioned General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Mr. Bilobrk.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you or your colleague Mr. Mikulic take any notes during that interview?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you take any notes?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Mikulic took any notes?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I believe he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What did you do with these notes? Did you keep them after the Official Note is prepared? Or where can they be now?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Once we drafted the Official Note, our handwritten notes stayed behind in the notebook that we had. You see, we don't have an obligation to keep our handwritten notes since these are only brief annotations of what the individual interviewed says and we use them to subsequently write Official Notes. We are not under an obligation to keep these notes. And if we were, I really don't see where we would put them all. In other words, I can't tell you where these notes I made can be found now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But you are certain that you made notes during that interview?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I'm absolutely sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show P2732, which is the Official Note that you and your colleague Mr. Mikulic prepared. Can you, please, first confirm that that is the note and look at whether this is your signature on the last page?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, this interview note is dated 9 November. And it states that the interview was conducted on 5 November. Now, bearing in mind that the 5th of November was a Thursday and that the note was prepared the following Monday, is that the general practice in terms of the length time between an interview and the preparation of the Official Note?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: You see, in this case specifically, I can tell you the following: After having conducted the interview with about Markac Bilobrk, we had another interview, either in Split or in Sibenik, and we weren't able to write the Official Note on that same day. The following day, we had another interview. Saturday and Sunday are not working days. And we wrote the Official Note on Monday as we got back to Zagreb. Had it had been possible, we would have written it sooner.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Who prepared this Official Note? And by that I mean who -- who typed it up?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when you signed it, did that mean that it accurately reflected what had occurred during the interview?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you or your colleague Mr. Mikulic light up a cigarette close to the window of the room where you had the interview?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: With Mr. Bilobrk?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I certainly didn't. I'm not a smoker. If anyone did, then it must have been Mr. Mikulic. But I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you tell Mr. Bilobrk that this was an informal interview and that no Official Note would be prepared?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, Mr. Bilobrk testified in this Court, and he categorically denied to this Chamber telling you and your colleague that General Cermak told him to place weapons next to the bodies in Grubori. Do you have any comment or any response to this?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, I don't. My only comment is that I accurately reflected Mr. Bilobrk's words in the Official Note. And it is his right to state whatever he wants before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me read you a portion of Mr. Bilobrk's testimony and ask you if you have any comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm referring to transcript reference 28724, starting at line 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The question was put to him: "Had you ever said to them" -- meaning you and Mr. Mikulic, "that General Cermak had suggested placing guns next to the dead bodies at Grubori?" His answer: "No. They came to me with that information. That's what they suggested. "Q. And how did they suggest that to you? Describe what happened in the time that you spent with them. How did they suggest it? "A. During that conversation, or while we conversed, rather, I can't remember which one of them mentioned that first. I can't repeat the words verbatim. "In any case, what they said was this. We came by information that General Cermak offered, or suggested, that you should place weapons by the dead bodies. "Q. And what did you say to that, when that was stated by one of them? "I told them that Mr. Cermak never said that to me, and it would have been strange if a person whom I saw for the first time among a group of people to say that to me. It would have been totally strange and didn't make much sense to imagine that somebody I saw for the first time came up to me and said, Take weapons and place them by the dead bodies." Now, Mr. Gerovac, the way Mr. Bilobrk described the interview, is that the way that the interview was conducted?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No. This is completely inaccurate. Let me repeat. At no point in time did we put a leading question to Mr. Bilobrk, in the sense of telling him a name or leading him, either toward Mr. Cermak or anybody else, in connection with the part which had to do with the engineering or the placing of rifles in Grubori. At no point during the interview did we put anything of the sort to him, suggest things to him that would lead him to mention General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what is the general rule -- or your general practice regarding making suggestions in an interview.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, you see, this isn't a rule only in our police force. It is a rule of the police in general that leading questions are not to be put. We did not give any sort of hints to Mr. Bilobrk to let him know what is the answer we would like to get. We did not say that any of the high-positioned MUP officials said something like that. We didn't mention a name or a person, anything that would lead him to present such a description of the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Would have you anything to gain by putting inaccurate information in an Official Note of interview?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No gain whatsoever. And I would never include in an Official Note something that the interviewed person didn't state.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you now -- just changing slightly topics. Can you briefly describe for us the interview you had with Mr. Vrticevic. Did you put similar types of questions to him than you did to Mr. Bilobrk at the beginning of his interview?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can give to you P2735. And if you can confirm for us that that is, in fact, the Official Note of interview of Mr. Vrticevic.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you also type that Official Note?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I can't remember at this point whether it was me or my colleague. I really can't remember at this point whether it was my colleague Mikulic or I.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you remember if you took notes in the interview with Mr. Vrticevic?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I think I did, just as I did in the case of Mr. Bilobrk.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, looking at this interview note, I'm not going to read a portion to you. It's in evidence and everyone here is quite familiar with it. First, there is a suggestion, the same question that you put to Mr. Bilobrk regarding high-level officials making the suggestion to place or leave weapons next to the bodies. And then he answers that he does not remember but allows for that possibility. And after that, in that case, you did specifically suggest certain names to him. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Right -- that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gerovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Those are my questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly. Mr. Kay, will you be the first one to cross-examine Mr. Gerovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour. Did -- is it the time now? I've forgotten what the schedule was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The schedule was from 2.00 to a quarter to 4.00 then have a 25 minutes' break and then to have another session of one hour and 20 minutes before we would move to the last session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kay. Mr. Kay is counsel for Mr. Cermak. Mr. Kay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, you said, in answer to a question from the Prosecution: "We did not give a hint to Mr. Bilobrk to let him know the answer we would like to get. We did not say that any of the high-positioned MUP officials said something like that." I would like you to now see Exhibit P2732, which is the Official Note you wrote of Mr. Bilobrk. If you could look at the text where it says: "After Jozo Bilobrk was informed of the need for a repeated preliminary interview ..." And it refers to the killing of civilians in Grubori. "New facts have been established which suggest that during the first preliminary interview he didn't provide all the facts in his possession regarding that event." And then the text reads: "The above was asked if it had been suggested to him and to his colleague, Ivica Vrticevic, who was working with him as a crime technician on the humane clearing up of the dead bodies of civilians killed in the village of Grubori, by somebody from the then-senior commanding structures of the MUP ... of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia that they should have conducted an on-site investigation in the village of Grubori but that before that they should have placed guns next to the dead bodies of civilians who had been killed in order to make it appear as if they had put up resistance to members of special police." That is what is in your Official Note as the first question that was asked of him. And it does contain a suggestion as to the identity of the person that you are interested in, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, in what way? You tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, first of all, when you were answering the questions of the Prosecutor, you said it wouldn't be right to suggest and you wouldn't -- did not say that any high-positioned MUP officials said something like that because that would be leading your witness to the answer that you wanted. In that passage that I have just read out to you, you have broken the rule that you said you would not break by, first of all, saying, Somebody from the then-senior commanding structures of the MUP ... or the Ministry of Defence, that they should have conducted an on-site investigation in the village of Grubori. And then you lead into the passage, which is the disputed passage, about placing guns next to dead civilians. Don't you agree, this Official Note written by you actually reflects something you said you would not do and did not do?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, I don't agree. Why? Had I or my colleague Mikulic put the following question: Did General Cermak or any other person named by us tell you to do such and such a thing, this is something that I would have considered a leading question. But I had to put the question to Mr. Bilobrk in some way that would make it clear to him rather than ask him, Did somebody suggest that you do something on that day. This sort of question would lead us nowhere. I had to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, you were very specific because you identified the person, saying that they should have conducted an on-site investigation in the village of Grubori. So you were being very specific, even on this note, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I must admit that I don't understand your question. Can you clarify, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You identify the person because you say it was somebody who said they should have conducted an on-site investigation but that before that they should have placed guns next to the dead bodies of civilians. So if anyone had said they wanted an on-site investigation, you were linking that with the placing of guns by the bodies of dead civilians.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No, I don't think at all that by saying -- and I'll read the relevant part. It is stated here that it was suggested from the higher positions in the MUP and MORH that an on-site investigation needed to be carried out. I don't see in what way this question put by me and Mr. Mikulic revealed the identity of these individuals. I really don't see how this can be considered a leading question. But -- especially if we know that only a superior could have ordered him to carry out an on-site investigation, not his subordinate. It had to be someone he considered to be his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Not at all. Because in the proposition you put here, first of all, it is not officials; it says somebody. It is a single person. Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No. It is actually a plural.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It then says that they should have conducted an on-site investigation in the village of Grubori; but before that, they should place guns next to the bodies of civilians, et cetera. So it refers to a distinct conversation about an on-site investigation, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: In my view, no. This is something that was supposed to have been done before an on-site investigation. I'm only conveying Mr. Bilobrk's words or, rather, what we had learned even before, unofficially though. We tried, in a way, to lead as little possible and indicate anyone. Perhaps it wasn't the best way to put it. But personally, I don't think either myself or Mr. Mikulic suggested any answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, doesn't it, in the very fact, in the fourth line of the English, so, near the beginning of this text in the Croatian, after it refers to the village of Grubori: "New facts have been established which suggest ..." So you were making or your colleague was making a positive suggestion, which is an opposite to what you've just said. The word "suggest" is there.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No. We did not put up any suggestions. We only told Mr. Bilobrk that there was new information that came about during our criminal inquiries, indicating that during his first interview he did not share all of his knowledge with the interviewers. And I don't see how we suggested anything to him by having said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only told him that we had knowledge making us conclude that he was not fully honest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, we read in this Official Note that you have informed Mr. Bilobrk that new facts had been established. And then it describes what those new facts would have been, including that somebody from the then-senior commanding structures of the MUP or the RH would have suggested or would have said that guns would have to be placed next to the dead bodies. Now, if you listened well, you may have noticed that I just read from the Official Note and that I did not refer to any name, although to a quality of the persons who would have suggested that. Is that what you put to Mr. Bilobrk during this interview as new facts that had come to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to be completely clear now. After having said to Mr. Bilobrk that during our criminal inquiries we had learned that during his first interview he did not share the full extent of his knowledge, we then moved on to the question. We did not share that information with him. We simply introduced him to the situation, and we told him what I wrote down. We said that during our criminal inquiry we learned that he may not have shared the full extent of his knowledge. And it was followed by our question as is stated in the text. At no point in time did we mention either Mr. Cermak's name or any other names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the substance of the information we read here, that there had been a suggestion to put weapons next to the bodies, that is what you told Mr. Bilobrk you had learned during your investigations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also that it was suggested, although you did not give any names, by a then-senior commanding -- somebody from the senior commanding structures of the MUP of the Croatian Republic or the Ministry of Defence of the Republic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, I earlier said that we can have lengthy debate on what makes a question leading or what makes anything suggestive. I think, first of all, we should focus on the -- on the facts, which I tried to do. If you have any further questions in this context, please put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour for -- for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And you did not even ask Bilobrk at the start of this interview what he had omitted to say earlier; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Look, I can't recall each and every second or minute of that conversation. What I put to him as a question and what was discussed is what found its way into my Official Note. I can't recall any other specific things, and I cannot say with any certainty whether I did or did not ask something. What is in my Official Note is based on my personal notes of what I said. Now that you are asking me this, I can tell you that I cannot recall now, off the cuff, whether such a question was put to him or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, do you agree, from looking at that text, which I've just read out in full once and nearly twice, that there is no evidence there of you asking him, first of all, before this passage, the open question of what, if anything, he had omitted to say in his earlier interviews. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes. This is not in the Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And, in fact, although you say you don't suggest answers to witnesses, you did the very same thing to Mr. Vrticevic, because, in his questioning, as recorded in the Official Note, it was put to him whether the suggestion had come from Zeljko Sacic or General Ivan Cermak. That was explicitly put to him. Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Of course, I did. We are not prohibited from putting a specific question. But had I put that question as the first question, that would not have been good. After he said that he cannot recall this, and that he thought that he might have, I put a specific question. There is no prohibition against putting such a question. I think he also said that he cannot remember that either and this closed the topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So this note shows that you do, in fact, suggest names to witnesses when you interview them for an Official Note, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: This is your opinion. Yet again, I can only say that myself or any other police official are entitled to put specific questions in cases in which further clarification is needed. Otherwise, without that, things would never be cleared up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it's not right to say that you don't give hints to witnesses to know -- to let them know the answer you would like. That's not right, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I try my utmost not to do that ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I notice the time. That might be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you give us an indication as to how much time would you need after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Within half an hour I will be finished, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: 15 minutes to half an hour, all depending on what happens before me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break, and we'll resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, what did you write your notes --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Please hold. Please hold. Please hold.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, the notes of interview of what was said between the police and Mr. Bilobrk at the time of the interview, what did you write those notes in or on?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I kept my notes on A-4 sheets of paper. They were put together in a very thin note pad which had a blue cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And where are those notes now?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: [In English] I don't know. [Interpretation] I don't know. I really don't. In any case, in the note pad there were some notes from other cases as well, not this one alone. I don't keep all of my notes. I've already said that. Because we are under no obligation to keep our personal notes. The only important thing is to draft an Official Note and to convey the information we had noted down in our note pad as accurately as possible into the Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Isn't it right that notes are kept of what is said between the police and the witness, that the notes taken at the time are kept?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: What notes exactly do you mean? You have to be more precise. The notes typed out on a computer? Or the notes we kept for ourselves during interviews?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The notes written at the time in the interviews.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No, we are under no obligation to preserve those. If you mean the notes I write in pen or pencil when I receive answers to my questions, we are under no obligation to keep them and we are under no oblige to archive them anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So is there no record at all, other than what you typed up as the Official Note, as to what was said at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer. The interpreter did not understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, Mr. Gerovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. In case I did not find the notes I kept in conversation with Mr. Bilobrk, which I kept save for the Official Note that is before me, based on those notes, there would be nothing else. However, I have to say yet again that we had no obligation keep our notes. It was only important to have them reflected as accurately as possible in an Official Note, which then had to be signed by us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, could I just intervene on one matter. You said you don't know where they are. They once were in a blue note pad. Now, did you -- did you look for them, did you search for them, did you ... did you try to find them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did. Because before coming here, I was asked whether I'd be able to locate those notes. I tried, but, unfortunately, failed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was unclear to me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was that? When did you try to find them?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly, but, say, a month back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And where did you look?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: In my office. But, unfortunately, I didn't find any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to Mr. Vrticevic's interview, are there any notes in existence from the day he was questioned?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't find those either. I cannot recall whether I kept any notes then because I was there with Mr. Mikulic and he may have kept the notes of the interview with Mr. Vrticevic. But, in any case, I couldn't find any notes in relation to Mr. Vrticevic's interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because Mr. Bilobrk has stated that you took no notes at the time, when you met him at the police station.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to say. Mr. Bilobrk says one thing; I say another. This is how it is. Perhaps if I can clarify something else. The Official Notes -- Note, under our Law on Criminal Procedure represents no evidence, and I gain nothing by adding or omitting anything. For the umpteenth time I can tell you this: I drafted the Official Note based on what Mr. Bilobrk told me and nothing else. Apparently Mr. Bilobrk later on down the road said something else, but I'm telling you that we did keep notes -- we made notes during interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you hear that Mr. Bilobrk had said something else down the road? When was that?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I don't understand. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said: Apparently Mr. Bilobrk said something else down the road, but I'm telling you we did make notes -- we made notes during interviews. What are you referring to there? I may have misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: You misunderstood. Apparently you put to me that Mr. Bilobrk said we kept no notes. In response to that, I told you that this was his view of that interview, proposing facts contrary to what I'm telling you. I simply say this was not the case. That is all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Wasn't this the position, Mr. Gerovac, that you, with Mr. Mikulic, met Mr. Bilobrk at the police station and just said you were passing by and wanted an informal chat with him.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: That is not true. I'll tell you what the procedure is. Given that he was a police employee, the procedure was this: One of our superiors called his superior, be it the head of the crime police or the crime sector, notifying them that on a particular day we were to arrive at the Split-Dalmatia Police Administration in order to conduct an interview with him. There was no informal conversation with Mr. Bilobrk. This was nothing that would have been done of our own accord. This must have been announced beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And it was suggested to him by you police officers that General Cermak had made a statement concerning placing weapons by the dead bodies, that that suggestion came from you and your colleague to him.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it the case, because you'd suggested it to Mr. Vrticevic, that General Cermak or Zeljko Sacic had said it, that, in fact, at the interview or meeting with Mr. Bilobrk you just came out with that straight away and said that to him.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No. You have the Official Note of the interview with Mr. Bilobrk. We only asked him whether Mr. Sacic was there with Mr. Cermak, because, if I'm not mistaken, he had mentioned it in his previous interview. His answer was that he cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... were you referring to the interview with Mr. Vrticevic, or were you referring to the interview with Mr. Bilobrk? Because the question -- no, let me just -- no, I made a mistake. I ... I made a mistake. I apologise. I withdraw what I said. Please proceed. If you want to put the question again to the witness, Mr. Kay, of course, you're free to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, I was just following to see if there was anything ambiguous in question or answer, Your Honour, and I'm satisfied with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiries or investigate the truth of the background, then, that you say Mr. Bilobrk gave you, that he was in Knin on the steps of the police station with other colleagues and General Cermak approached him with the suggestion to place weapons at the crime scene? Did you investigate where Mr. Bilobrk was on that day; where he went; whether that meeting could possibly have taken place?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, undoubtedly Mr. Bilobrk was in Knin on that day because he was at the Knin Police Administration, waiting to set out for the clearing of terrain operation in Grubori. Based on his statement and based on Mr. Vrticevic's statement, they said, as is contained in their notes, that they were in the Knin Police Administration at the time. And this did not call for additional evidence. As for the very encounter with Mr. Cermak, we were not able to clarify this bit fully, in terms of finding other individuals who may have been present during that conversation, either from among the colleagues who were there or those who were accompanying Mr. Cermak. If your question had to do with the latter part, we were not able to clarify this bit; in other words, to gain additional information from individuals who may have been present during the event described by Mr. Bilobrk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, those are my questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kay. Mr. Kuzmanovic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, it's Mr. Kuzmanovic who will now cross-examine you. Mr. Kuzmanovic is counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Gerovac.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor which was dated March 3rd of this year. Do you have that statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, now it's working.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We'll get it on the screen in a moment, as soon as I get the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I can assist, it's 65 ter 7668.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could please get that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it to come up on the screen, Mr. Gerovac, you can read the Croatian version, it will be coming up soon on the left. Paragraph 2 and 3 I'm referring to specifically. Paragraph 2 notes that: "We reviewed the notes" --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2, please, of the English and the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: "We reviewed the notes of the interviews with Jozo Bilobrk and Ivica Vrticevic taken in October 2009 ..." Who is "we"? There is no identification of -- other than I'm assuming you are one of the "we"?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the other person?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You note further in that paragraph in the fourth line: "The fact that in one of them they were told not to reveal anything damaging to the generals was obviously problematic." Now I will refer you, Mr. Gerovac, to P2731.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could get that on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: P2731, Mr. Gerovac, is the 13th of October, 2009, Official Note taken of Mr. Vrticevic and Mr. Bilobrk together by Mr. Badzim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if we go to page 2 of the English. And I believe -- if we could scroll down on the Croatian, if we can go to the next page of the Croatian, please. Actually, I do think -- I'm sorry, I apologise. I think it's on the first page of the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The particular passage I would like to focus on starts -- this is in relation to the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. This passage in P2731 says: "They also would like to emphasise that the Defence team asked to be notified of any subsequent requests for information regarding the talk that they had. Because of the circumstances in which they gave their statements to the Defence team about a month ago, Vrticevic and Bilobrk declined to describe the clearing of terrain in the village of Grubori in detail, as it could damage the generals." Now, you would agree with me, Mr. Gerovac, there's nothing in those two sentences that I read that says anything that Mr. Bilobrk or Mr. Vrticevic were told not to reveal anything damaging to the generals.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In this passage that I just quoted to you, Mr. Gerovac, nowhere in that passage does it state that Mr. Bilobrk or Mr. Vrticevic were told by anyone - specifically Mr. Djurica or anyone else - not to reveal anything damaging to generals. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: That's correct. There isn't anything specifically indicating that they should not say anything. But, rather, that they should contact the Defence as soon as somebody asked to interview them, if I understand this correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. But in your ICTY statement that you gave to the OTP, you say: "They were told not to reveal anything damaging." That's not correct, is it? In light of the passage from the October --

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In light of the passage that I read to you from October of 2009, your statement that they were told not to reveal anything damaging to the generals as it relates to the first October 2009 statement is not correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: You see, we could deal with it at the level of a play of words. But the following passage states the following, and it's connected with the other one: Because of the circumstances which arose a month earlier when they gave a statement to the Defence, so it relates back to what was said earlier on, they do not wish to speak in detail about the events in Grubori because this might be damaging to the general. So, you are right; nobody banned them from speaking. It is they themselves who chose not to say anything, and than's what I was able to glean from this statement now for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling me this is the first time that you saw the Official Note of Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic taken by Mr. Badzim?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No. You misheard me. I said that that would -- that was my interpretation and would have been my interpretation when I saw it for the first time. And this is the umpteenth time that I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so my question to you is: Do you agree with me, or do you disagree with me that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, could you make a break now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's just that the record's not being preserved because Mr. Kuzmanovic -- I know he is listening in the original language, but obviously there is a -- it creates a problem for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, it's important that everything is recorded, what someone says, isn't it? You --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- understand the great importance of that, so please secure that it happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I will do so, Your Honour. I was listening in Croatian, and I will now listen in English. So I will wait for the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, it's very easy for us to cut each other off because we each may know where we're going. So please let me answer my question -- ask my question -- and I will do best to let you answer before I continue with my next question. Because if we talk on top of each other, it's difficult for the translators to keep up, as well as the transcriber. All right. I will go back to my original question relating to your statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor where you state in paragraph 2: "They," meaning Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic, "were told not to reveal anything damaging to the generals." And I think you agree with me that at least in the October statement, P2731, there is no indication that anyone told them not to reveal anything damaging to the generals. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Nobody told them that they were not allowed to do that. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you under the impression that Mr. Vrticevic gave a statement and/or met with the Defence team of General Markac in August of 1995 [sic]?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think Mr. Kuzmanovic may want to read the question on the screen, and he may want to reformulate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The year is incorrect. August of 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you under the impression that Mr. Vrticevic gave a statement and/or met with the Defence team of General Markac in August of 2009, last year?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, you see, I can be under no impression whatsoever. I can either know something or not. Based on this statement, evidently they met. They did meet, and this is something that we knew for the following reason: The Defence team asked for permission to meet with him. So they spoke to him, but I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... did you ask Mr. Vrticevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ask Mr. Vrticevic whether or not he met with the Defence team of General Markac in August of 2009?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in August of 2009 Mr. Vrticevic was on vacation and did not meet with the Defence team of General Markac at any time?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we pull up P2730, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: P2730 is an October 20th statement, Official Note of Mr. Bilobrk only. And this was again taken by Mr. Badzim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if we go to the last page of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The sentence I'm referring to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have a technical problem. We'll have to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's all my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For all those who thought that I wouldn't know what to do, I do know, meanwhile. The Chamber will withdraw but will remain stand by and hopes that within a couple of minutes the matter will be fixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for your information, I don't have very much to go. I have one more statement after this one review and then I'll be done. So it won't be very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I take it that you want to have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, I'd first like to put on the record that we stopped because of technical difficulties, that the Chamber then decided to have a short break and to remain stand by. And I do understand, I think for the eighth or the tenth time today, that we had overcome the technical difficulties. And optimistically we proceed. You, the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, we'll go back to P2730. Again, referencing first your statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor where you said you reviewed the notes of the interviews with Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic taken in October 2009. We've gone over the first of those notes. This is the second of those notes. The second section -- or the last two sentences of this Official Note taken by Mr. Badzim says -- of Mr. Bilobrk, says: "He was asked by the General's Defence team in August this year to make a statement on the clearing up of the terrain in Grubori, together with Ivica Bobinac, but since Bobinac was not present in Grubori, he did not make any statements. The interview focussed solely on the Grubori event, and there was no discussion of any other events." Now, Mr. Gerovac, if you had, in fact, read the notes of the interviews in October 2009, you could have come to the conclusion that the only person with whom the Markac Defence met in August of 2009 was Mr. Bilobrk. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: It's not correct. You -- you have a note where the two of them say that they spoke with the Defence team. Can we go back to the earliest note.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you do anything to clear up that discrepancy, to find out if, in fact, Mr. Vrticevic had met with the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, I don't see what is unclear here. Doesn't the first note, the one that include two interviewees, state that both of them said to have met with members of the Defence team? You can find the note.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that wasn't my question.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take to Mr. Bobinac at all?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Mikulic?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: You should have asked him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: And I'm telling you, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In this October, latter October, Official Note, which you said you reviewed, again, there's nothing in this latter October Official Note - 2730, P2730 - that says anything that "they were not told to reveal anything damaging to the generals." That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I've already said that the note reads that they were suggested -- that it was suggested to them that before they take part in any interviews concerning Grubori, they should notify the Defence team and that before they've contacted them, they should not make any statements. That's what I said. Now, whether I was misunderstood when I was giving my statement to the OTP, I don't know. But I repeat: It was suggested that they should, before taking part in interviews concerning Grubori, contact the Defence team. Again, they were told to notify them before giving statements on Grubori.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... thanks for that answer, Mr. Gerovac, but that's not what I asked you.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Very well. Then we don't understand each other apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, I've got no idea what your question was. Look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The question is: In P2730, which is in front of you on the screen, an Official Note taken of Mr. Bilobrk, dated October 20th, 2009, which you said you reviewed before taking another interview of Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic, there's nothing in this document that says either of those gentlemen were told not to reveal anything damaging to the generals. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that question has put now two or three or four times to the witness. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like an answer though, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first of all, what a document says or not is for everyone to read. And I think we went through it quite a bit. Whether that -- it says that or whether it gives other facts which would allow or not allow for certain conclusions is another matter. But I think the witness, until now, everything you put to him what is specifically found in the text of a document, he has, until now, answered all your questions that this is not what specifically the document says and then he sometimes added certain portions of information which he apparently considered to be relevant in that context. Now, whether it's relevant or not is still to be seen. But let's -- the question, Do you agree that the letter A does not appear, or letter B, or letter X, or letter Y, or letter Z does not appear in this text, is really something that should not be further explored at this moment. If you have any questions in relation to that matter, please put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to P2732, which is the November 9th, 2009, Official Note, another one of Mr. Bilobrk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, the last paragraph of that particular Official Note that you and Mr. Mikulic took says nothing about the witness not to reveal anything damaging to the generals; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As part of your investigation, Mr. Gerovac, did you talk or interview Mr. Cetina? Talk to or interview Mr. Cetina?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you or anyone that you know of talk to anybody in the crime police department in the police administration of Zadar-Knin in 1995 related to Grubori?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No. I don't know about that. I don't know if anybody did talk to them or -- and, if so, when. If you're referring to the senior staff, the then-senior officers, there may have been, yes, interviews; but when and who with, by whom, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you -- do you -- did you find out who, if -- who was the direct person in charge of Mr. Vrticevic and Mr. Bilobrk in August of 1995? And, if so, did you speak with them regarding this Grubori incident?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Unless I'm mistaken, I'll try to remember. They were seconded. They were operating in the then-Zadar-Knin Police Administration, assisting other policemen in the clear-up operation. I really can't remember who their superior was, and I'm talking about the immediate superior of the two of them. Is that what you're asking me about? I know who the head of the Zadar-Knin Police Administration was at the time. That was Mr. Cetina. But I can't recall who the immediate superior of Mr. Bilobrk and Mr. Vrticevic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If -- I know you can't recall a name, but did you speak with whomever that person was?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I definitely did not. Perhaps if I had been able to review any documents, I may have been able to answer this. But, otherwise, I can only speculate about whether anyone spoke to that person and when. It is a large case file and certainly not the only one. I really can't remember each and every person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was the Zadar Police Administration, their criminal investigation section, the section that was responsible for conducting an on-site inspection in Grubori in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Yes. Given that in terms of territory, the area of Knin - and I don't think I'm wrong - fell under the Zadar administration. Although, at the time - I'm trying to jog my memory - the -- the Knin-Kotor district had its seat in Knin, and I remember that they had scene-of-crime officers come in from Zadar since there was no such a team in Knin. Both the police and the investigative judge from Zadar were competent to carry out an on-site investigation in Grubori.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to Mr. Badzim, you worked together with him on this investigation at some point; correct? Relating to the current investigation, I mean.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that Mr. Badzim gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in which he stated that the state attorney, Mr. Bajic, instructed the crime police specifically to investigate command responsibility issues in Grubori in June-- starting in June of 2009?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the contents of Mr. Badzim's statement. I know he did give a statement; however, I do know that the state attorney, Mr. Bajic, requested of the police chief in question to launch an investigation into the Grubori case. And that request is still on our file. Specifically, there were two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did that deal with command responsibility investigations?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: Well, look, I cannot recall the contents of the request. Command responsibility was definitely not the only issue. It also had to do with discovering the perpetrators. The request did not specifically mention only those who may have been within the chain of command and responsible for the area, but it also had to do with the discovery of perpetrators. I'm definitely positive that it wasn't command responsibility alone that was requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, one moment and I'll be -- just to confer with counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. May I take it that the Gotovina Defence, same position? Mr. Hedaraly, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No need to re-examine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, I have - although very few - questions for you. Could we have on the screen P2732. First page. And it is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, the first lengthy paragraph, which is the fourth paragraph of the statement, a little bit down from the middle of that paragraph, I see a few words in the original. And forgive me for not pronouncing them properly. [B/C/S spoken] Do you see those words? Is that the language which refers to putting weapons?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, what I'd like to know is that the word "postave" is used. Could I -- before you answer, let me first phrase my question. Is there any chance that you have misinterpreted what Mr. Bilobrk has said, and that he, rather, expressed a view which is better reflected by the word "ostave" rather than "postave"?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No. It is precisely as is stated here, to place the rifles in the sense that a third party should bring those rifles in and place them there in order to give away an impression of a combat. So not to leave them, but to place them. I don't know whether this is sufficiently clear. I can try and explain in even more detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What I'd like to know is whether you remember that he used that word or whether you are convinced that this reflects what he said because of the context which is given in this Official Note. So do you remember the word he used; or is that, in this context, you consider that "postave" is what he meant?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No. I remember him explicitly saying "to place." Did he not use any other words. To place the rifles. Had he said to leave them, that's what would have been in the -- in the note. This is precisely what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
