utterances.text: Yes. We receive, of course, your words now translated into English. But I take it that those who are interpreting your words were interpreting that he said "postave" and not "ostave."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. One final question: It took a while before the interview taken on the 5th of November was put on paper. The Official Note dates from the 9th of November. Do you remember who you interviewed in between? Because you said you didn't put it on paper because you had another interview, I think, you even referred to possibly Sibenik. Could you -- do you remember who you interviewed between the 5th or still on the 5th and the 9th?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Mikulic and I, the next day or perhaps on the same day in the afternoon or in the evening, went to Zadar where we spent the night. The next day we had an interview, I believe, with Mr. -- I can't recall his name. He is still employed with the Zadar Police Administration in their department or group tasked with war crimes. I don't recall his name right now, but I do know that at the time of these events in Grubori, he also worked in the area of Knin or was seconded to Knin from Zadar. That is why we went to see him. However, I really can't tell you his name now. As for the period between the Friday in Zadar, it wasn't only Mr. Mikulic and I there, but there were other two work-mates of ours in charge of interviews. Well, in the evening, after all these interviews, we went back home. Given that we did not work over the weekend, only on our arrival to work on Monday did we sit down and draft the Official Note. That's the only reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was not asking about reasons; I was asking about who you interviewed meanwhile. Was that one interview of that person whose name you do not remember, or were there more interviews conducted by you?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I don't think it was the only interview. There must have been at least two, I believe, that Mr. Mikulic and I conducted. Although I'm not 100 percent certain. I think there were at least two. However, I can't tell you who the persons in question were and whether there were any more interviews than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, even if you do not remember the name of one of the interviewed persons, do you by any chance have a recollection on whether the issue of putting the weapons next to the bodies was an issue which was part of the interview you conducted before that Monday?

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: No. Those questions were not put to these persons, at least to those I can remember being interviewed by me and Mr. Mikulic. Based on what we had learned so far, in terms of the intelligence we had, it indicated that they did not have any knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any further question triggered by the questions by the Bench? Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, the persons that you may have interviewed in the interim, were they Mr. Krvavica and Mr. Raspovic perhaps? Ivan Krvavica and Slavko Raspovic in Sibenik -- no, in Zadar, I mean.

utterances.speaker: ANTONIO GEROVAC
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Krvavica was not interviewed then. It is possible, though, that Mr. Raspovic was. I don't recall Mr. Krvavica. I don't recall him being interviewed on that day or the day before. I really can't recall now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no further questions, this concludes your evidence, Mr. Gerovac. One question -- before we say farewell to you, I would like to ask you to follow the usher just for perhaps not more than half a minute or two minutes and to just wait outside the courtroom and then we'll see you back in a minute from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The reason why I asked the witness to leave the courtroom is, Is there any need to re-call either Mr. Bilobrk or one -- any of the witnesses who are on stand by? Let's keep it short.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Not for us, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And not for us, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber also feels no need to ask further questions, to put further questions to the other witnesses. Could the witness be brought into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gerovac, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for answering the questions that were put to you by the party and by the Bench. And I hope that you have a safe trip home again. I'm not going to instruct you that you should not speak about your testimony because although it will be in a short written decision that the testimony of you and some other witnesses will be -- the non-public status will be lifted. Therefore, this really concludes, now, your testimony. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could the Victims and Witness Section be instructed to convey the message to all three witnesses, that is, Mr. Bilobrk, Mr. Gerovac, and Mr. Mikulic, that they're not under an order anymore, that they should not speak with anyone about their testimony. They're free to do so if they wish. As I said before, unless there would be any opposition by the parties, but I would expect the opposite, as a matter of fact, the confidential status should be lifted, and, as I said before, this will be put down in the short written decision. Then I think the Chamber invited the parties to -- to point at where the word "postave" was used and where perhaps another expression is used; I don't think that I have to set a deadline for that, but could we expect this within the few days to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll meet -- we'll send something to the Cermak Defence and get their agreement. I doubt it will be controversial. So I'm sure we can give it to the Chamber in a few days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. Mr. Mikulicic, I think we, earlier today, we inquired as to whether you intend to call any further witnesses in response to the witnesses that were called by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are not going to call anyone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that, Mr. Kay, would, an estimate that next Thursday and Friday would be sufficient to hear the evidence of the witnesses you intend to call?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, as originally indicated, I think it's a two-day section of court evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I have no further procedural matters on my agenda. Is there anything to be raised? Then we adjourn, and we -- we resume on Thursday, the 10th of June, at 9.00 in the morning, in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
